subject.title: [Feature Request] Unified Built-in Sandbox with Multi-Platform Support and Tiered Presets

question: What first milestone should maintainers approve for OpenClaw's core sandbox architecture: secure-by-default presets, plugin process isolation, manifest policy enforcement, or a narrower tool/backend milestone first?
rationale: The current code has partial opt-in tool sandboxing, but changing default isolation and plugin execution boundaries is a security, compatibility, and product-direction choice that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Keep canonical and split milestones
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella tracker, then create maintainer-owned milestone issues for the first approved sandbox boundary and migration plan.

options.title: Narrow to tool sandboxing first
options.body: Defer native plugin process isolation and use this issue only to coordinate tool/backend hardening until plugin runtime boundaries are designed separately.

options.title: Reject core default change for now
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide secure-by-default sandbox presets are not planned for core and should remain opt-in/backend-specific.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical and split milestones
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella tracker, then create maintainer-owned milestone issues for the first approved sandbox boundary and migration plan.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already supplied the keep-open architecture review and Peter Steinberger authored major sandbox backend groundwork.
